assertion.name: Karyotype Analysis
assertion.description: Definitive diagnosis rests on demonstrating complete or partial absence of a second sex chromosome. Because mosaicism is common and can be tissue-limited, a normal peripheral-blood karyotype does not exclude the diagnosis in a clinically suspicious case — which is why the guideline specifies a minimum of 30 metaphases rather than a standard count, and why a normal blood result in a phenotypically suspicious individual is followed by analysis of a second tissue.

assertion.name: Hepatitis B Serologic Panel Interpretation
assertion.description: Initial hepatitis B screening uses three tests together (the triple panel): HBsAg, antibody to HBsAg (anti-HBs) and total antibody to hepatitis B core antigen (anti-HBc, which detects IgM and IgG). The combination separates current infection, resolved infection, vaccine-derived immunity, susceptibility and isolated core antibody: HBsAg with total anti-HBc and without anti-HBs indicates current infection, acute when IgM anti-HBc is also present and chronic when it is absent; anti-HBs with total anti-HBc and without HBsAg indicates resolved infection; anti-HBs alone indicates immunity from vaccination. IgM anti-HBc is ordered only when acute infection is a concern.

assertion.description: A reduced GAA activity result with no pathogenic genotype may reflect a pseudodeficiency allele rather than disease. The best-characterized example is GAA c.271G>A (p.Asp91Asn), which depresses measured enzyme activity but has been formally reviewed as benign for Pompe disease. assertion.notes: The preprint additionally reports a patient homozygous for c.271G>A whose symptoms were ultimately explained by a PABPN1 variant, which is the clinical shape of the error this entry is guarding against.

assertion.name: TNFRSF11A Exon 1 Duplication Testing
assertion.description: Molecular confirmation is a heterozygous in-frame 18-bp tandem duplication in exon 1 of TNFRSF11A, found in every FEO kindred published. Because the lesion is a small tandem duplication in a GC-rich repeated sequence, the assay must be duplication-sensitive: Sanger sequencing of exon 1 in both directions, or a skeletal-dysplasia panel that provides deletion/duplication analysis alongside sequencing, detects it; a pipeline that does not resolve small tandem duplications can miss it. The length of the duplication identifies the allelic disorder (27 bp for early-onset familial Paget disease, 15 bp for expansile skeletal hyperphosphatasia, 12 bp for panostotic expansile bone disease), so the test also settles the differential among the RANK signal-peptide disorders. Parental testing distinguishes inherited from de novo duplications, and cascade testing identifies at-risk relatives before skeletal lesions form. Unexplained multiple external root resorption in a child is a recognised trigger for testing.
assertion.results: Heterozygous 84dup18, or the one-base-shifted 18-bp duplication, in exon 1 of TNFRSF11A.

selected_evidence.snippet: It is recommended that when ERR cannot be explained by local etiologic factors, systemic abnormalities and genetic testing should be considered.

assertion.name: Temporal-Bone CT and MRI with Audiometry

diagnosis_term.preferred_term: high-resolution temporal-bone CT with MRI and audiometry

assertion.description: Audiometry and tympanometry characterise the hearing loss, which is conductive at first and later mixed, and coronal high-resolution CT of the temporal bones shows the state of the ossicular chain, from hypoplastic and dysmorphic ossicles to their complete absence. assertion.name: Clinical Recognition of the Deafness, Root Resorption and High-Turnover Osteolysis Triad
assertion.description: The diagnosis is suspected from the stereotyped sequence: conductive hearing loss from early childhood, external root resorption and premature loss of the permanent teeth in adolescence, and from the second decade painful expansile osteolytic lesions of the limb bones on a background of raised bone-turnover markers with normal calcium and phosphate. assertion.name: Skeletal Radiography

diagnosis_term.preferred_term: plain radiography of the limb bones

assertion.description: Plain radiographs of symptomatic sites, or a skeletal survey, show the two classes of change described in the original kindred: generalised alteration of the trabecular pattern and modelling of the long bones, which can be seen before any focal lesion, and focal lytic areas that enlarge along the shaft, expand the bone and thin the cortex until the medulla is replaced by fibrous and then fatty tissue. selected_evidence.snippet: In contrast to classical PDB, the pelvis, spine and skull were unaffected.

assertion.description: Gold standard diagnostic test for CF. Pilocarpine iontophoresis stimulates localized sweating; sweat is collected and chloride concentration measured. Chloride >=60 mmol/L is diagnostic, 30-59 mmol/L is intermediate, <30 mmol/L is CF-unlikely.

reference_ranges.notes: Two of the three boundaries come from the consensus itself and one from a guideline that adopts it: the 2017 CF Foundation nonscreened-population paper states that the intermediate threshold was lowered from 40 mmol/L to 30 mmol/L, and the 2025 Australasian sweat-testing guideline, written to align with the international consensus, states the intermediate result as values between 30 and 59 mmol/L for all ages and 60 mmol/L or more as supportive of a diagnosis of CF. The 2017 De Boeck and Vermeulen review words the confirmatory value as "above 60mmol/L", one point off the consensus "60 or more"; the band keeps the consensus boundary and the discrepancy is disclosed here rather than shifted. The half-open bands put exactly 30 in the intermediate band and exactly 60 in the diagnostic band, which agrees with both guideline statements.

assertion.name: Adult global consensus clinical diagnosis
assertion.description: Diagnose ARDS when acute or worsening hypoxemic respiratory failure occurs within one week of a predisposing insult or new respiratory symptoms, with bilateral loss of lung aeration on radiography, CT, or qualified ultrasound, and edema not primarily explained by cardiac failure, fluid overload, collapse, effusion, or embolism. Hypoxemia can be identified by PaO2:FiO2 at or below 300 mm Hg or by SpO2:FiO2 at or below 315 when SpO2 is at or below 97%; the global definition includes specified nonintubated and resource-limited pathways. Nonintubated criteria require HFNO at least 30 L/min or NIV/CPAP with at least 5 cm H2O end-expiratory pressure. Intubated criteria require PEEP at least 5 cm H2O. A separate resource-limited category does not require a specific oxygen-delivery device, flow or PEEP. Cardiogenic edema and chronic lung disease can coexist when they do not primarily explain the acute hypoxemia.
assertion.results: Acute bilateral noncardiogenic inflammatory lung injury with qualifying hypoxemia supports the diagnosis; severity and respiratory-support category should be recorded separately.

assertion.name: Serum Anti-Mullerian Hormone with Gonadotropin and Androgen Panel
assertion.description: Serum AMH, measured alongside inhibin B, testosterone, LH and FSH. AMH partitions the two genetic subtypes rather than establishing the diagnosis: a low or undetectable value points to the ligand gene and a normal or elevated value to the receptor gene. A normal AMH therefore does not exclude PMDS, and reading it that way is one of the routes to a missed diagnosis. Tumour markers are added when a mass is present.
assertion.results: Low or undetectable serum AMH in PMDS type I; normal or elevated serum AMH in PMDS type II.
assertion.notes: The two directions are curated as separate subtype-attributed records in the biochemical section, where the discrepancy between them is the informative content.

assertion.name: Semen Analysis
assertion.description: Assessment of the ejaculate in an adult, and the first step of the fertility workup. Where the excurrent ducts are intact and at least one testis is scrotal, spontaneous paternity is possible, so the result decides whether sperm can be banked from the ejaculate or must be sought by testicular extraction. assertion.name: AMH and AMHR2 Sequencing with Copy-Number Analysis
assertion.description: Sequence and deletion/duplication analysis of both genes. Copy-number detection is specified rather than assumed because AMHR2 microdeletions occur, and a whole-gene deletion in trans with a point variant makes that variant look homozygous on Sanger sequencing alone - so a sequencing-only result can be both wrong about zygosity and wrong about which parent is a carrier. A wider disorder-of-sex-development panel or exome is appropriate when first-line testing is negative, and a negative result does not exclude the pathway. assertion.name: Lymphocyte subset flow cytometry
assertion.description: The first-line immunological test, and the one that places the disease beside ZAP70 deficiency rather than with the other causes of infantile autoimmunity. It shows reduced CD8 T cells with a raised CD4:CD8 ratio, and in the sister an increase in CD19 B cells. The deficit is partial, so the panel does not read as a SCID.
assertion.notes: Newborn T-cell receptor excision circle screening was normal in both children, so a normal TREC result does not exclude this disease. That is the same caveat that applies to ZAP70 deficiency, where continuing CD4 thymic output can keep the screen normal.

selected_evidence.snippet: Immunological workup revealed mild T and B cell lymphopenia in the brother and reduced CD8 T cells in both affected children, resulting in an elevated CD4/CD8 ratio

selected_evidence.snippet: was later diagnosed by endoscopy as inflammatory colitis, similar to that of her brother

assertion.name: Molecular genetic testing (exome sequencing)
assertion.description: The definitive test, and how the disease was found. Exome sequencing of five family members identified the compound heterozygous ZAP70 genotype and the carrier state of the healthy relatives. Both alleles were private to the family, so sequencing alone leaves two variants of uncertain significance: the functional work on zeta-chain binding and on autoinhibition is what makes the result interpretable.

selected_evidence.snippet: Whole-exome sequencing performed on five family members revealed the affected siblings to be compound heterozygous for two unique missense mutations in the 70-kD T cell receptor ζ-chain associated protein (ZAP-70).

reference_ranges.notes: This is the general ISCD reporting threshold for densitometry in children and adolescents, not a PLS3-specific cut-off; the disease does not own it, and it is recorded here because the Z-score, not the adult WHO T-score, is the scale on which affected boys are measured.
